account_policy.native_ubuntu: Ubuntu/OpenSSH passwd/shadow/group/gshadow, system users and SSH credentials remain outside the ASUS mount namespace. No SSH credential synchronization is performed.
account_policy.asus: Original create_passwd/create_custom_passwd/create_ovpn_passwd semantics and UID/GID assignments are preserved in a private /etc overlay; NAS/FTP/PAM/OpenVPN consumers inherit that exact namespace and files NSS view.
account_policy.failure: All guarded account entrypoints and the rc dispatcher exit125 if private overlay identity is absent. No host identity fallback or successful no-op.
account_policy.atomicity: Vendor account writers retain their original multi-file update behavior. This implementation prevents host corruption; it does not claim transactional updates of the four private account files.
account_policy.custom_hooks: JFFS passwd/shadow/group hooks execute inside the private view. They remain privileged trusted code and are not confined against deliberate /proc/1/root access.

namespace.propagation: recursive slave: child mounts do not propagate to host; existing persistent and runtime mounts remain the same objects
namespace.persistent_requirement: /data and /jffs must already be writable mounts; production rejects tmpfs/ramfs/overlay.
namespace.private_shell: verified /usr/libexec/asus/ash binds read-only onto canonical /usr/bin/dash only in child namespace
namespace.private_preload: /usr/$LIB/leon-asus/libleon-rc-notify.so; both native and armel package libraries required; ABI expansion/loading proof owned by root
namespace.hosts: private /etc/hosts symlinks to /run/asus/etc/hosts, allowing libc files NSS and dnsmasq to see the same dynamically regenerated ASUS table
namespace.nsswitch: private files passwd/group/shadow/gshadow; hosts files dns; no systemd identity injection into vendor view

kernel.requirement: native manager loads the exact kernel10 overlay module before launcher

remaining_integration: Native package wiring and actual board-specific rc build/link remain required.
Vendor units started separately by systemd do not automatically inherit this mount namespace; explicitly join the rc namespace before activation.
Private /etc lower includes Ubuntu defaults, not all missing ASUS /rom/etc defaults; seed required vendor config files explicitly.
Existing JFFS/data mounting, BCM boot scripts, mdev/hotplug2 and direct hardware operations still require ownership integration.
No new network namespace: ASUS DHCP/DNS/firewall still share host networking and require explicit service ownership.
Old generation directories remain in volatile /run until reboot; a safe stopped-service cleanup policy is still required.
This is mount ownership separation for trusted root services, not a sandbox for malicious vendor code.

runtime_fixture.scope: Host kernel user/mount/PID namespace plus empty synthetic chroot, production launcher compiled but not run. Test launcher permits synthetic persistence mounts with a fixture marker. Parent namespace and etc identity use read-only bind references because subordinate usernamespace cannot read /proc/1/root; production keeps real PID1 reference paths.

command:
set -eu
leon_private_root=$(mktemp -d /tmp/asus-private-etc-root.XXXXXXXX)
cleanup() {
 umount -R "$leon_private_root/proc" 2>/dev/null || :
 umount "$leon_private_root/run" 2>/dev/null || :
 umount "$leon_private_root/data" 2>/dev/null || :
 umount "$leon_private_root/jffs" 2>/dev/null || :
 umount "$leon_private_root/fixture-origin-etc" 2>/dev/null || :
 umount "$leon_private_root" 2>/dev/null || :
 rm -rf "$leon_private_root"
}
trap cleanup EXIT
mkdir -p "$leon_private_root/etc" "$leon_private_root/proc" "$leon_private_root/run" "$leon_private_root/data" "$leon_private_root/jffs" "$leon_private_root/persistent-data" "$leon_private_root/persistent-jffs" "$leon_private_root/usr/bin" "$leon_private_root/usr/libexec/asus"
ln -s usr/bin "$leon_private_root/bin"
ln -s dash "$leon_private_root/usr/bin/sh"
cp "$1/launcher" "$leon_private_root/launcher"
cp "$1/probe" "$leon_private_root/probe"
cp "$1/ash" "$leon_private_root/usr/libexec/asus/ash"
cp "$1/busybox" "$leon_private_root/usr/libexec/asus/busybox"
cp "$1/dash" "$leon_private_root/usr/bin/dash"
for abi in aarch64-linux-gnu arm-linux-gnueabi; do mkdir -p "$leon_private_root/usr/lib/$abi/leon-asus"; done
cp "$1/shim-arm64" "$leon_private_root/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/leon-asus/libleon-rc-notify.so"
cp "$1/shim-armel" "$leon_private_root/usr/lib/arm-linux-gnueabi/leon-asus/libleon-rc-notify.so"
printf 'root:x:0:0:Ubuntu root:/root:/bin/sh\nubuntuonly:x:1000:1000:Ubuntu user:/home/ubuntuonly:/bin/sh\n' > "$leon_private_root/etc/passwd"
printf 'root:!native-locked:1:0:99999:7:::\nubuntuonly:!native-locked:1:0:99999:7:::\n' > "$leon_private_root/etc/shadow"
printf 'root:x:0:\nubuntuonly:x:1000:\n' > "$leon_private_root/etc/group"
printf 'root:*::\nubuntuonly:*::\n' > "$leon_private_root/etc/gshadow"
printf 'passwd: files\ngroup: files\nshadow: files\nhosts: files\n' > "$leon_private_root/etc/nsswitch.conf"
printf '127.0.0.1 localhost\n' > "$leon_private_root/etc/hosts"
printf 'native-persistent-configuration\n' > "$leon_private_root/etc/fstab"
printf 'nameserver 192.0.2.1\n' > "$leon_private_root/etc/resolv.conf"
chmod 600 "$leon_private_root/etc/shadow" "$leon_private_root/etc/gshadow"
touch "$leon_private_root/ASUS_ETC_LAB_FIXTURE"
mount --bind "$leon_private_root" "$leon_private_root"
mkdir "$leon_private_root/fixture-origin-etc"
mount --bind "$leon_private_root/etc" "$leon_private_root/fixture-origin-etc"
mount -o remount,bind,ro "$leon_private_root/fixture-origin-etc"
mount -t proc proc "$leon_private_root/proc"
mount -t tmpfs -o mode=0755 tmpfs "$leon_private_root/run"
mount --bind "$leon_private_root/persistent-data" "$leon_private_root/data"
mount --bind "$leon_private_root/persistent-jffs" "$leon_private_root/jffs"
(cd "$leon_private_root"; sha256sum etc/passwd etc/shadow etc/group etc/gshadow etc/nsswitch.conf etc/hosts etc/fstab etc/resolv.conf usr/bin/dash) > "$leon_private_root/protected-before"
chroot "$leon_private_root" /probe --outside
chroot "$leon_private_root" /launcher --leon-systemd
chroot "$leon_private_root" /probe --outside
(cd "$leon_private_root"; sha256sum etc/passwd etc/shadow etc/group etc/gshadow etc/nsswitch.conf etc/hosts etc/fstab etc/resolv.conf usr/bin/dash) > "$leon_private_root/protected-after"
cmp "$leon_private_root/protected-before" "$leon_private_root/protected-after"
test ! -e "$leon_private_root/etc/ld.so.preload"
test ! -e "$leon_private_root/etc/.asus-private-etc"
test ! -e "$leon_private_root/etc/pam-private-fixture"
test -s "$leon_private_root/persistent-data/shared-proof"
test -s "$leon_private_root/persistent-jffs/shared-proof"
test -s "$leon_private_root/run/shared-proof"
grep -qx '/usr/$LIB/leon-asus/libleon-rc-notify.so' "$leon_private_root"/run/asus/etc-ns/generation.*/upper/ld.so.preload
umount "$leon_private_root/data"
status=0
chroot "$leon_private_root" /launcher --leon-systemd || status=$?
test "$status" = 125
echo LAB_PRIVATE_ETC_HOST_PROTECTED_AND_MISSING_DATA_REFUSED_PASS

target_runtime_fixture.scope: Real kernel10/systemd PID1, production mount checks and real PID1 references; only backend is synthetic. Private ext4 is an image wholly inside guest RAM, no host disks or NIC.
target_runtime_fixture.production_guards: Real PID1 namespace and /proc/1/root/etc references; production ext4 mount checks; only backend path is replaced by benign probe.
verified: Actual guest ext4 block-device UUID accepted and atomic boot/device/inode attestation consumed before and inside the ASUS namespace.
Wrong UUID rejects with status125 and removes a previously valid attestation; removing mounts invalidates previously valid proof.
ASUS private passwd/shadow/group lookups and regenerated hosts work without modifying nine protected Ubuntu files or adding host ld.so.preload.
A native dynamic child loads the private notify shim, sees private NSS, and executes through matching ASUS ash with inherited signal mask cleared.
Writes to data, jffs and run remain shared; the launcher refuses missing persistence mounts.
Native journald, udev and dbus remain active; real systemd PID1 completes the fixture.
limitations: No actual ASUS rc/service/hardware execution; synthetic account operations exercise the same guard and libc/NSS interfaces.
ARMEL shim is a checked prerequisite but this fixture runs no ARMEL program; ABI-specific preload proof is separate.
Fixture data and jffs deliberately share one guest-RAM ext4 filesystem; actual board UUID policy is still unset.
No real router device, secret, network interface or persistent storage is passed through.
